segments.he: בזמן הר' נחמן מטולטשין ז"ל היו אנשים שבאו חזרה מארץ ישראל ובתוכם גם מאנ"ש והיו מדברים מהפירות שלא נתיישר בעיניהם ואמרו שבשם דהיינו בארץ ישראל אוכלים עשבים (והיו יכולים לחשוב שאוכלים עשבים כמו בהמות. ואפשר הי' כמנותם כמו שעושין עתה כמה מטעמים מהעשבים) ושמע הר' נחמן מטולטשין ז"ל ורגז עליהם מאד וסתר את כל דבריהם וקרא אותם בשם מוציאי דיבה (מוציאי דיבייניקע'ס) ובילה כמה זמן לשבח הפירות מארץ ישראל ואמר הלא אני בעצמי הייתי שם וממש כל דבר יש לו טעם גן עדן ובפרט השמן זית וכו' וכן פרט הכל בפרוטרוט וכו':
segments.en:
Once there was a story at the Remak [Reb Moshe Cordovero], of blessed memory — one of the ancient Gaonim and decisors. He walked in the marketplace and stood among the fruit sellers, took a fruit from the finest of the fruits of a gentile standing there — made a blessing and ate it, then ate another and another. The gentile became very angry and beat him with severe blows. Immediately the gentile became dangerously ill and his head turned backwards and he could not speak — [people understood this had come because he struck the Rabbi]. The Remak stood there astonished as to why he was being beaten. Meanwhile all the street came and begged him to forgive the gentile and pray for his healing. He was amazed — for he had no idea what had happened. He had been so absorbed in Torah thoughts and the service of G-d that he did not know he was in the marketplace at all. He only saw fruit lying before him and thought he was in his own home and that his wife had placed fruit for him to eat. And so he made a blessing and ate — and suddenly he was being beaten. He forgave the gentile and prayed for him — and he was healed.

And similarly there was a story with a certain Gaon — Reb Yokil Hamburger who was a Chief Rabbi. Once a visitor in the house of study placed his walking stick near the Holy Ark and could not find it. He saw the Rabbi there and suspected him [not knowing he was the Rabbi, since the Rabbi was walking about in plain clothes] — and hit him, demanding the stick back. The Rabbi kept begging: "I did not see your stick and did not take it." The visitor did not believe him and kept hitting him. Afterward the Rabbi had to ascend the platform to deliver a sermon — and delivered it with great brilliance and sharpness. The visitor was standing there and now saw whom he had suspected and beaten. He came up to the platform to beg forgiveness. But the Rabbi — when he finished his sermon and saw this same man on the platform — thought he was coming to beat him again over the stick! And he began again to beg him: "Believe me — I truly did not take your stick, I never touched it at all!" Then the visitor explained that he had come to beg forgiveness — for when he saw him preaching on the platform he came to make peace.
